info.title: Ergoly platform API
info.description:
Read and change one organization's own Ergoly environment. Every route is scoped to the organization the presented credential resolves to; there is no parameter that widens it. The human-readable reference is served from the same namespace at `/api/v1/docs`, behind the same credential.

The namespace's front door is `GET /api/v1`, and it is deliberately absent from `paths` below. It answers without a credential — what this API is, how an organization admin mints a key, and where the reference lives — so it is the way in to this contract rather than a part of it: it has no scope, takes no parameters, and there is nothing about it for a generated client to call. Every `unauthorized` refusal carries that same URL as `error.docs`.

The row exists when this returns and a provisioning run has started; poll `jobId` at `/api/v1/jobs/{id}`. When `currentStep` is `await_oauth_install`, open the job's `installUrl` in a browser as a Slack workspace admin — nothing here can finish that step for you. Approving it starts a second run, so follow the rest on `GET /api/v1/workers/{id}`, whose `latestProvisioningJob` is always the current one. `slug` must be unique in your organization, and a handful of words control uses in its own URLs are reserved.

**Provisioning mints a Slack app, a sandbox and an agent. It costs money and spends one of your organization's daily provisioning slots.**

get.description: Every place on your Company chart a Worker may sit under — a person's seat, a Worker's, a team, an open role — in the order the chart draws them, each with its title and the place it sits under. Pass one's `id` as `reportsTo.placementId` when you create a Worker. Nothing inside a vendor or a client is listed, because a Worker may not sit there. The whole chart comes back at once; it is not paged.

For a key that was minted for a Worker, this is that Worker — the same record and the same fields as `/api/v1/workers/{id}`, without needing the id. It is the call to make first, because a Worker's own id is what almost every other call takes: its channels and its eworks. A key held by a person rather than by a Worker answers 404: there is no Worker for it to be, which is not a permission that could be granted. Address a Worker by its id instead.

delete.description:
The Worker stops serving immediately and drops out of every list here. Its Slack app configuration is left behind for an admin to remove by hand — the install is revoked, the app is not deleted.

**This tears down real infrastructure and cannot be undone. Every ework under the Worker has its sandbox and its agent destroyed, the Slack install is revoked, and the Worker's scheduled jobs stop firing. Nothing here rebuilds it: a replacement is a new Worker, with a new agent that remembers none of this one's work.**

post.description:
Creates that pair's client-tier ework and, in the same call, optionally maps channels and binds people to it. The routing rows are durable when this returns; `activation` says whether the agent behind them came up. A channel or a person already bound to a different Client is refused rather than re-pointed. Channels the bot could not join are reported in `joinFailures` and do not fail the call.

**Binding brings up a client-tier ework — a sandbox and an agent. It costs money and spends one of your organization's daily provisioning slots.**

post.description:
Opens a Slack channel on the CALLING worker's own identity, so only a worker's key can call it. It creates the room, maps the caller, maps then invites each of `workers`, and invites the person who asked — the sender of the caller's running turn, never a body field — then `people`. With no person asking it is a 409 before any room exists. Each of `people` must be a person of the org's own Slack, else a 409 (`person_outside_org`, `person_not_a_person`, `person_lookup_failed`) before any room exists. Anyone who could not be brought in is reported, not failed.

**A `client` mapping brings up that Client's ework for each Worker mapped to the room, and spends one of your organization's daily provisioning slots. An `internal` room mints nothing.**

post.summary: Invite a worker to a channel
post.description: Mapping a channel decides where its traffic routes; this puts the bot in the room, which is the other half and the one Slack will not do by itself. Only a worker's own key can call it, and the invite is made on that worker's own bot token and nothing else. The Worker being added must already be mapped to the room — map first, then invite; an unmapped room is a 409 `channel_not_mapped`. It acts only for a member: the room must already hold the calling worker's bot AND the person who asked — the sender of the calling worker's running turn, read on control, never named in the request. The calling worker never joins a room. Otherwise the call is a 409 whose `reason` says which: `inviter_not_in_channel`, `requester_not_in_channel`, `no_human_requester` (nobody's request is running — a scheduled run, a webhook) or `requester_unclear` (more than one is). A person in the room can then add the worker themselves: `/invite @worker` in the channel, or the channel's settings, then Integrations, then Add apps. A bot that is already there answers 200 with `invited: false`, so a retry is safe. The call takes no body; a body naming any field is a 400.

post.description: Without `scheduleKind`, opens a task held by the Worker in `workerId`, with an optional `description` and `dueAt`; the Worker is woken by it. With `scheduleKind`, schedules a job instead. `scheduleKind: "once"` takes an ISO `runAt`; `"cron"` takes a five-field `cronExpr` and a `timezone`. A `client`-tier job needs a `clientId`. An unrecognized zone is refused rather than replaced with a default — you meant a specific wall-clock time, and running a 09:00 job at 09:00 UTC instead is the kind of wrong nobody notices for a week.

post.description: Two shapes, told apart by `app`. WITHOUT it, this stores a secret: `value` is write-only, it goes in here and no route gives it back; give at least one host unless the key already has some — a credential no host points at is never injected by the gateway, so it would sit there doing nothing; a key already taken at the same scope is a `conflict`, as is a host already mapped to another connection. WITH `app` — a catalog slug or a tool server's URL — this connects an app and places it: omit `auth` and the answer carries `connectUrl`, a hosted sign-in to open in a browser, with the connection `pending` until consent finishes and `active` after (poll `GET /api/v1/connections/{id}`); send `auth.mode: "key"` with the key in `value` and it is stored at Composio and checked with one real call, `verified` reporting the verdict; a tool server that takes a key names the header it goes in with `auth.header` (absent is `Authorization`, sent as `Bearer <key>`; any other header carries the key on its own); a tool server that takes no credential is `auth.mode: "none"`, and gets a row and a placement with nothing stored anywhere. A `placement` no ework could read — `instance` on a Worker with no active ework for that Client, `client` for a Client no Worker has one for — is a `conflict` naming the pair, refused before a key or a sign-in reaches Composio. The check is made once, up front: an ework removed while Composio is being called can still leave the placement in place, and adding or moving a placement later is checked again at the write. `connectUrl` is shown once — a replay under the same `Idempotency-Key` withholds it — and the pasted key is never in any response. `sessions` says which eworks can use the app now.

What this does depends on what the connection is. A plain secret is deleted, and its host mappings come down with it if no other variant of the key survives. A connected OAuth account is DISCONNECTED: the token is revoked with the provider first, which is the part that matters, then the row and its hosts go. A provider app is refused — remove it through its own route, which also cleans up every account connected with it. A CONNECTED APP is revoked at Composio first and then removed with every placement it had; `outcome` is `revoked` or `removed` (matching `revoked`), and `sessions` says which eworks lost it. An app Composio cannot revoke programmatically (Exa; a tool server's own sign-in) is still `removed`, with `revokeNotSupported: true`: revoke the credential at the vendor. Any other revoke Composio could not confirm is an `upstream_error`, and the connection stays.

**This removes a credential your agents may be using. A disconnect also revokes the token at the provider, which cannot be undone — reconnecting means going through consent again.**

invited.description: Did this call add it? False when it was a member already.

alreadyInChannel.description: It was already there, so nothing was done.

method.description: How the calling Worker's own bot did it — `bot_token` (it invited the bot). Null when nothing had to be done.

joined.description: Always false: the calling Worker's bot never joins a room. It invites only into a room it AND the person who asked are already in, and that is already mapped for the Worker being added; otherwise the call is refused (409, `reason` `inviter_not_in_channel`, `requester_not_in_channel` or `channel_not_mapped`).

requestedBy.description: The Slack id of the person the invite was made for: the sender of the calling Worker's running turn, read on control. Never a request field — the call takes no body, and a body naming any field is a 400.

clientSlug.description: The Client the room's work belongs to; null for an internal room.

requestedBy.description: The Slack id of the person who asked: the sender of the calling Worker's running turn, read on control and never a body field. Always among `people` — they are brought in first. A call no person made (a scheduled run, a webhook) is refused before the room exists (409, `reason` `no_human_requester` or `requester_unclear`).

caller.description: The calling Worker, which created the room and is in it.

kind.description: How the calling Worker is mapped. Always `internal` for an internal-only Worker.

activation.description: For a `client` mapping, whether that Client's ework is serving yet.

error.description: Why this Worker is not mapped or not in the room. Null when it is.

code.description: A machine code: a mapping refusal (`internal_only_worker`, `requires_confirmation`, …) or an invite refusal (`invite_refused` — Slack refused, carrying its code, …).

message.description: What happened, in words to pass on.

mapped.description: Did its mapping land? A Worker that is not mapped is not invited.

activation.description: For a `client` mapping, whether that Client's ework is serving yet.

invited.description: Did this call add its bot?

method.description: How the calling Worker's own bot did it — `bot_token`.

error.description: Why this Worker is not mapped or not in the room. Null when it is.

code.description: A machine code: a mapping refusal (`internal_only_worker`, `requires_confirmation`, …) or an invite refusal (`invite_refused` — Slack refused, carrying its code, …).

message.description: What happened, in words to pass on.

workers.description: One entry per Worker named in `workers`.

people.description: One entry per person brought in: the person who asked, first, then each named in `people`.

cancelled.description: Always true. The row is soft-deleted, so its run history survives.

sha.description: Its new blob sha. Pass it as `expectedSha` on the next write.

changed.description: False when the content was already identical, so nothing was committed.

created.description: True when the file did not exist before.

notified.description: How many running eworks were told. Null when nothing needed telling.

commitSha.description: The single commit that carried them.

Webhook.description: An inbound URL that starts a turn.

id.description: The webhook id. It is also the URL segment deliveries are POSTed to.

workerId.description: The Worker whose agent takes the delivery's turn.

clientId.description: The Client whose scope owns this webhook. Null on a core-scoped one, which is what a key creates. Where its deliveries run is `workClientId`.

workClientId.description: Null when the work is no one client's: an internal room, a DM, a task whose targets name several clients, or a revoked webhook, which has let go of its task (`taskId: null`). Otherwise the Client whose work each delivery is, read from its task: a webhook on a room mapped to a client runs on that client's agent.

name.description: What this endpoint is called. It is what the agent is told the delivery came from.

description.description: Free text for whoever maintains it.

url.description: Where to POST. Absolute, so you need no base URL of your own.

surface.description: Where the worker posts each delivery's result.

kind.description: A room, or a direct message with one person.

channelId.description: The Slack channel id, on a `channel` webhook.

slackUserId.description: The Slack user id, on a `dm` webhook.

threading.description: The older way to set `runMode` and `keepMemory`. `top_level` and `new_thread` behave alike: events overlap, each run with its own conversation. `same_thread` runs events one at a time on the task's one shared conversation; it is not one Slack thread.

taskId.description: The task each delivery starts a run on. Its destination is where results go; null once a revoke has let go of it.

runMode.description: `overlap` runs events side by side, each with its own conversation. `one_at_a_time` runs them in turn on the task's shared conversation.

keepMemory.description: True when every event run shares the task's one conversation, so a later event remembers an earlier one. Implies `one_at_a_time`.

threadTs.description: Unused: nothing reads or writes it.

rootText.description: Unused: stored, and nothing reads it.

promptTemplate.description: What the agent is asked to do, with the payload appended below it — or placed at `{{payload}}` when the template names that. Null uses the built-in wording.

enabled.description: False once it is disabled or revoked. Every delivery to a disabled endpoint answers 410.

createdBy.description: Which surface minted it. Audit only; nothing behaves differently.

lastDeliveredAt.description: When it last accepted a delivery.

revokedAt.description: When it was retired. A revoke is a one-way door.

secret.description: The delivery credential, SHOWN ONCE. A `whsec_…` secret goes as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` on every POST; a `whlnk_…` secret (link mode) rides in `link`. It is stored hashed, so this is the only time it can be read — store it now, or rotate.

link.description: Link mode only, and absent otherwise: the URL with the secret in it (`?token=whlnk_…`), for a sender that takes a web address and cannot set a header. SHOWN ONCE. The link is the credential: treat it like a password.

url.description: Unchanged — a rotation does not move the endpoint.

secret.description: The new credential, SHOWN ONCE: `whsec_…` for a header, `whlnk_…` in link mode. The previous secret, and any previous link, stopped working the moment this was issued; there is no overlap.

link.description: Link mode only, and absent otherwise: the URL with the secret in it (`?token=whlnk_…`), for a sender that takes a web address and cannot set a header. SHOWN ONCE. The link is the credential: treat it like a password.

WebhookDelivery.description: One inbound POST, as the ledger recorded it.

id.description: The delivery id, as the 202 returned it.

payloadBytes.description: How big the body was. The body itself is not stored.

status.description: `accepted` started a turn. `pending` was claimed and its turn is still starting. The rest did not start one — `error` says why.

error.description: Why it was not accepted. Null on `accepted`.

envelopeId.description: The turn it started. Null when none was.

channel.description: Where the worker posted this delivery's result: the Slack conversation, or the person's user id for a direct message. Null until it posts.

threadTs.description: The thread it posted under, or its message when top-level. Null until it posts.

idempotencyKey.description: The caller's own retry key, when it sent one.
